In [[abstract algebra]], a '''conjugacy class sum''', or simply '''class sum''', is a [[function (mathematics)|function]] defined for each [[conjugacy class]] of a [[finite group|finite]] [[group (mathematics)|group]] ''G'' as the sum of the elements in that conjugacy class. The class sums of a group form a basis for the [[center (algebra)|center]] of the associated [[Group ring#Group algebra over a finite group|group algebra]].

== Definition==
Let ''G'' be a finite group, and let ''C''<sub>1</sub>,...,''C''<sub>''k''</sub> be the distinct conjugacy classes of ''G''. For 1 ≤ ''i'' ≤ ''k'', define

:<math> \overline{C_i}=\sum_{g\in C_i}g.</math>

The functions <math>\overline{C_1},\ldots,\overline{C_k}</math> are the class sums of ''G''.

== In the group algebra ==
Let '''C'''''G'' be the [[complex number|complex]] group algebra over ''G''. Then the center of '''C'''''G'', denoted Z('''C'''''G''), is defined by

:<math>\operatorname{Z}(\mathbf{C}G) = \{f \in \mathbf{C}G \mid \forall g\in \mathbf{C}G, fg = gf \}</math>.

This is equal to the set of all [[class function]]s (functions which are constant on conjugacy classes). To see this, note that ''f'' is central [[if and only if]] ''f''(''yx'') = ''f''(''xy'') for all ''x'',''y'' in ''G''. Replacing ''y'' by ''yx''<sup>−1</sup>, this condition becomes

:<math> f(xyx^{-1})=f(y) \text{ for } x,y \in G</math>.

The class sums are a basis for the set of all class functions, and thus they are a basis for the center of the algebra.

In particular, this shows that the dimension of ''Z''('''C'''''G'') is equal to the number of class sums of ''G''.

==References==
* Goodman, Roe; and Wallach, Nolan (2009). ''Symmetry, Representations, and Invariants''. Springer. {{isbn|978-0-387-79851-6}}.  See chapter 4, especially 4.3.
* James, Gordon; and [[Martin Liebeck|Liebeck, Martin]] (2001). ''Representations and Characters of Groups'' (2nd ed.). Cambridge University Press. {{isbn|0-521-00392-X}}.  See chapter 12.
